docs.title: What is it?
docs.text: The Account Numbers feature automatically syncs employee/organization identification numbers from Mayo Clinic's BigQuery database into the Tableau Admin Dashboard. This makes it easy to identify users and correlate Tableau activity with employee records.

docs.title: The Process
docs.text:
BigQuery Database
    ↓
YOUR_USER_ACCOUNT_MAP_VIEW view
    ↓
Sync Service (Automatic)
    ↓
Tableau Admin Dashboard Users Table
    ↓
Displayed in Dashboard

docs.title: Data Sources
docs.text:
• Source: your-gcp-project.your_dataset.YOUR_USER_ACCOUNT_MAP_VIEW
  • Key Column: CLIENT_ACCOUNT_NUMBER
  • Match Field: User email address
  • Sync Frequency: Automatic when sync endpoint is triggered

docs.title: 1. Users Section
docs.text: In the Users page, each user listing includes: - User name - Email address - Account Number (employee ID) - Last login date - Site role

docs.title: 2. Custom Views Section
docs.text: In the Custom Views page, each view shows: - View name - Owner email - Account # (owner's employee ID) - Workbook/worksheet - Shared/private status

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Owner Email             | Account #
---|---
user.three@yourorg.com   | 1000001
user.two@yourorg | 1000004
smith.john@hca.org      | - (not found)

docs.title: When You See a Number
docs.text:
Example: 1000001

This means: - ✅ User has a Mayo Clinic employee account - ✅ Account number synced from BigQuery - ✅ Can be correlated with HR/employee records - ✅ User is internal Mayo staff

docs.title: When You See a Dash (-)
docs.text:
Example: -

This means: - ⚠️ No matching account number found in BigQuery - ⚠️ Likely an external user (contractor, partner, etc.) - ⚠️ Not found in employee database - ⚠️ May need additional security oversight

docs.title:
Mayo vs Non- Classification

Internal Accounts (@yourorg.com): - Email ends with @yourorg.com - Usually have account numbers - Internal Mayo employees - Full access to internal systems

Non- Accounts: - Email from other domains (external hospitals, consultants, etc.) - Usually DON'T have account numbers - External contractors/partners - Limited, role-based access - May require additional security clearance

Using the Account Type Filter

The Custom Views page includes a new filter:

[Account Type Filter ▼]
  ☐ All accounts
  ☐ <Org> only
  ☐ Non-<Org> only

Mayo Only

Shows custom views created by: - Users with @yourorg.com email addresses - Users with synced account numbers - Internal Mayo employees

Use cases: - Compliance reporting (internal vs external) - Usage analysis of Mayo staff - Access auditing for internal content

Non- Only

Shows custom views created by: - Users with external email addresses - Users WITHOUT synced account numbers - External contractors/partners - Other organizations

Use cases: - Monitor external user activity - Ensure external users have appropriate access - Track collaboration with partners - Security auditing of external access

1. Compliance Reporting

Scenario: Auditor asks "Who created this view? Is it an employee?"

Solution: 1. Go to Custom Views 2. Find the view 3. Check Owner Email and Account # 4. If account # is populated → Mayo employee 5. If "-" → External user (needs explanation)

2. User Identification

Scenario: Manager asks "Can you tell me about john.smith's usage?"

Solution: 1. Go to Users or Custom Views 2. Find by email 3. See associated Account Number 4. Match with HR database for full context 5. Report activity and recommendations

3. Access Control Audit

Scenario: Security team wants to ensure external users have limited access

Solution: 1. Filter Custom Views by "Non- only" 2. Review each external user's activity 3. Verify their access is appropriate 4. Check if they should have access to sensitive content 5. Take corrective action if needed

4. Collaboration Tracking

Scenario: How much content are external partners creating?

Solution: 1. Filter Custom Views by "Non- only" 2. Count views created by external users 3. Identify which external organizations 4. Assess value vs security risk 5. Plan collaboration governance

5. Organizational Reporting

Scenario: Executive wants to understand Mayo vs external user engagement

Solution: 1. Export Custom Views data 2. Filter by account type 3. Generate statistics: - % of views by Mayo vs external - Trend over time - By department/workbook 4. Present to leadership 5. Adjust strategy based on insights

Data Synchronization
  • Trigger: Manual or automatic sync endpoint
  • Update Frequency: On-demand
  • Match Logic: Email address (case-insensitive)
  • Success Rate: ~4,117 mappings found in BigQuery

Matching Algorithm 
For each user in Dashboard:
  Get user email
  Search BigQuery for matching email
  If found:
    Populate account_number
    Mark as internal if @yourorg.com
  Else:
    Leave account_number blank
    Mark as Non-<Org>

Data Quality
  • Coverage: ~4,117 account numbers synced
  • Accuracy: 100% (direct from BigQuery)
  • Freshness: Updates on demand
  • Availability: Covers Mayo Clinic employees

"I don't see account numbers"

Solution: 1. Refresh the page (Ctrl+R) 2. Wait for sync to complete (can take a few minutes) 3. Check if user email matches BigQuery records 4. Verify the user is a Mayo employee

"I see a dash (-) for a Mayo employee"

Causes: - Email address doesn't match BigQuery exactly - User was recently hired (not yet in BigQuery) - User has multiple email addresses - Account not yet synced

Solution: 1. Check email format 2. Verify in BigQuery directly 3. Wait for next sync 4. Contact IT if issue persists

"Account numbers aren't matching users"

Cause: Email addresses don't match between systems

Solution: 1. Check user's official email in directory 2. Verify against BigQuery 3. Update if inconsistent 4. Re-run sync

✅ DO
  • ✅ Use account numbers for compliance reporting
  • ✅ Filter by Mayo vs Non- when auditing access
  • ✅ Track changes in account assignments
  • ✅ Correlate with HR data for full context
  • ✅ Report metrics to stakeholders

❌ DON'T
  • ❌ Don't assume "-" means unauthorized access (could be new employee)
  • ❌ Don't make hiring/firing decisions based solely on account numbers
  • ❌ Don't ignore external users with high access
  • ❌ Don't forget to verify email addresses match

docs.title: FAQ
docs.text:
Q: What if I don't see account numbers? A: The sync may not have been run yet. Go to the Custom Views page and manually trigger the sync, or wait for the automatic sync to complete.

Q: Why do some users not have account numbers? A: They're likely external users (contractors, partners) not in the BigQuery employee database. This is expected and normal.

Q: Can I manually edit account numbers? A: The dashboard pulls directly from BigQuery for accuracy. To update, contact your BigQuery administrator to update the source data.

Q: How often is this synced? A: Sync can be triggered manually. Check with your Tableau Administrator for automatic sync schedules.

Q: Is this data secure? A: Yes. Account numbers are restricted data with appropriate access controls. Only authorized users can see this information.

docs.title: Key Terms
docs.text:
• Workbook: Tableau file containing dashboards and visualizations
  • Project: Organizational folder for grouping workbooks
  • Extract Status: Whether data is live-connected or cached on server
  • Stale: Workbook not updated in 90+ days (configurable)
  • Owner: User who created/owns the workbook

docs.title: Tableau Admin Dashboard - Daily & Weekly Check Schedule
docs.text: Complete guide for monitoring and maintaining your dashboard.

docs.title: 📅 Maintenance Schedule Overview
docs.text: Frequency Duration What to Check Status Daily 2 minutes Quick status Automated ✓ Weekly 5 minutes Health report review Automated ✓ Monthly 15 minutes Deep audit Manual Quarterly 30 minutes Performance review Manual

docs.title: When
docs.text:
• Best time: Early morning (8-9 AM) before team uses dashboard
  • How often: Once per day, Monday-Friday
  • How: Automated or manual

docs.title: Automated Daily Check (EASIEST)
docs.text: No action needed! The dashboard auto-restarts if it crashes.

docs.title: Manual Daily Check (If You Prefer)
docs.text:
Open PowerShell and run:

# Quick 30-second status check
Write-Host "Dashboard Status:" -ForegroundColor Cyan
$task = Get-ScheduledTask -TaskName "TableauAdminDashboard"
Write-Host "  Task: $($task.State)" -ForegroundColor $(if ($task.State -eq 'Running') { 'Green' } else { 'Red' })

Write-Host "Port Check:" -ForegroundColor Cyan
if (netstat -ano 2>$null | findstr :5000) { 
    Write-Host "  Port 5000: Listening ✓" -ForegroundColor Green
} else { 
    Write-Host "  Port 5000: NOT Listening ✗" -ForegroundColor Red
}

Write-Host "Browser Access:" -ForegroundColor Cyan
$web = Invoke-WebRequest -Uri "http://localhost:5000" -UseBasicParsing -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
if ($web.StatusCode -eq 200) {
    Write-Host "  Dashboard: Accessible ✓" -ForegroundColor Green
} else {
    Write-Host "  Dashboard: NOT Accessible ✗" -ForegroundColor Red
}

docs.title: What's Healthy?
docs.text: ✅ Task shows "Running" ✅ Port 5000 shows "Listening" ✅ Dashboard shows "Accessible"

docs.title: Issue: "Dashboard Not Responding"
docs.text:
Priority: 🔴 High (1 hour)

Steps: 

# 1. Restart the service
Restart-ScheduledTask -TaskName "TableauAdminDashboard"

# 2. Wait 30 seconds
Start-Sleep -Seconds 30

# 3. Test
Start-Process "http://localhost:5000"

# 4. If still fails, check logs
Get-Content "C:\Users\<your-user>\AppData\Local\nssm\TableauAdminDash\stderr.log" -Tail 50

docs.title: Issue: "Port 5000 Not Listening"
docs.text:
Priority: 🔴 High (1 hour)

Steps: 

# 1. Check what's using the port
netstat -ano | findstr :5000

# 2. Check if task is running
Get-ScheduledTask -TaskName "TableauAdminDashboard" | Select-Object State

# 3. Restart task
Stop-ScheduledTask -TaskName "TableauAdminDashboard"
Start-Sleep -Seconds 5
Start-ScheduledTask -TableName "TableauAdminDashboard"

# 4. Verify
netstat -ano | findstr :5000

docs.title: Issue: "Repeated Crashes/Restarts"
docs.text:
Priority: 🟠 Medium (4 hours)

Steps: 

# 1. Check the logs
Get-Content "C:\Users\<your-user>\AppData\Local\nssm\TableauAdminDash\stderr.log" -Tail 100

# 2. Look for patterns in error messages

# 3. If database issue:
Stop-ScheduledTask -TaskName "TableauAdminDashboard"
Remove-Item "C:\path\to\tableau-admin-dashboard\instance\cache.db" -Force
Start-ScheduledTask -TaskName "TableauAdminDashboard"

# 4. If dependency issue:
cd "C:\path\to\tableau-admin-dashboard"
.\.venv\Scripts\pip install -r requirements.txt
Restart-ScheduledTask -TaskName "TableauAdminDashboard"

docs.title: Issue: "High CPU or Memory Usage"
docs.text:
Priority: 🟡 Medium (8 hours)

Steps: 

# 1. Monitor usage
Get-Process python | Where-Object {$_.Name -eq "python"} | Select-Object Name, CPU, Memory

# 2. Restart for cleanup
Restart-ScheduledTask -TableName "TableauAdminDashboard"

# 3. Check if specific page causes issue
# Try accessing different pages in browser and note which uses resources

# 4. If problem persists, check logs for queries running too long
Get-Content "C:\Users\<your-user>\AppData\Local\nssm\TableauAdminDash\stdout.log" | Select-String "slow\|query\|processing"

The Tableau Admin Dashboard was successfully set up to run 24/7 as an automated Windows Service with:

docs.text:
Objective: Create a batch file that activates venv and runs the app

File: run_service.bat

Location: C:\path\to\tableau-admin-dashboard\run_service.bat

Content: 

@echo off
cd /d "C:\path\to\tableau-admin-dashboard"
call .venv\Scripts\activate.bat
python app.py

Creation Command: 

$DashboardPath = "C:\path\to\tableau-admin-dashboard"
$BatchContent = @"
@echo off
cd /d "$DashboardPath"
call .venv\Scripts\activate.bat
python app.py
"@

Set-Content -Path "$DashboardPath\run_service.bat" -Value $BatchContent -Encoding ASCII -Force

Why This Works: - cd /d - Changes directory (even if on different drive) - call .venv\Scripts\activate.bat - Activates the virtual environment - python app.py - Runs the application

docs.title: Step 3.2: Install Windows Service with NSSM
docs.text:
Objective: Register the dashboard as a Windows Service

Prerequisites: - ✓ PowerShell running as Administrator - ✓ NSSM installed at C: ools ssm ssm.exe - ✓ Batch wrapper created

Command: 

C:	ools
ssm
ssm.exe install TableauAdminDash "C:\path	o	ableau-admin-dashboard
un_service.bat"

Expected Output: 

Service "TableauAdminDash" installed successfully!

What This Does: - Creates a Windows Service named TableauAdminDash - Registers it to run the batch script - Sets it up in Windows Service Control Manager

docs.title: Step 3.3: Configure Service Properties
docs.text:
Objective: Set service behavior and options

Commands: 

$ServiceName = "TableauAdminDash"
$NssmExe = "C:\tools\nssm\nssm.exe"

# Set display name
& $NssmExe set $ServiceName DisplayName "Tableau Admin Dashboard"

# Set service to auto-start
& $NssmExe set $ServiceName Start SERVICE_AUTO_START

# Set to auto-restart on exit
& $NssmExe set $ServiceName AppExit Default Restart

# Set shutdown timeout (30 seconds)
& $NssmExe set $ServiceName AppThrottle 30000

# Configure logging
$LogDir = "$env:APPDATA\Local\nssm\$ServiceName"
& $NssmExe set $ServiceName AppStdout "$LogDir\stdout.log"
& $NssmExe set $ServiceName AppStderr "$LogDir\stderr.log"

What Each Setting Does:

Setting Effect DisplayName How it appears in Services GUI Start SERVICE_AUTO_START Starts automatically on boot AppExit Default Restart Auto-restarts if app crashes AppThrottle 30000 Waits 30 seconds before restarting AppStdout/AppStderr Logs output for debugging

docs.title: Step 3.4: Start the Service
docs.text:

Start-Service -Name TableauAdminDash

Get-Service -Name TableauAdminDash | Select-Object Status, StartType

Running Automatic

docs.title: Step 4.1: Create PowerShell Script for Starting App
docs.text:
Objective: Create a script that runs the app with auto-restart on crash

File: start-app.ps1

Location: C:\path\to\tableau-admin-dashboard\start-app.ps1

Content: 

# Use full path to python in venv
$pythonExe = "C:\path\to\tableau-admin-dashboard\.venv\Scripts\python.exe"
$appPath = "C:\path\to\tableau-admin-dashboard\app.py"

while ($true) {
    # Run the app
    & $pythonExe $appPath

    # If it crashes, wait 10 seconds before restarting
    Start-Sleep -Seconds 10
}

Why This Approach: - Uses explicit paths (no venv activation needed) - Auto-restarts on crash - Runs in infinite loop - Logs to Task Scheduler

docs.title: Step 4.2: Enable PowerShell Script Execution
docs.text:
Objective: Allow PowerShell scripts to run

Command: 

Set-ExecutionPolicy -ExecutionPolicy RemoteSigned -Scope CurrentUser -Force

What This Does: - Allows downloaded scripts to run - Still blocks dangerous scripts - Only for current user (safe)

docs.title: Step 4.3: Create Task Scheduler Job
docs.text:
Objective: Register a scheduled task that starts the app on boot

Prerequisites: - PowerShell as Administrator

Commands: 

# Define task details
$taskName = "TableauAdminDashboard"
$scriptPath = "C:\path\to\tableau-admin-dashboard\start-app.ps1"

# Create action (what to run)
$action = New-ScheduledTaskAction -Execute "powershell.exe" `
    -Argument "-NoProfile -WindowStyle Hidden -File `"$scriptPath`""

# Create trigger (when to run)
$trigger = New-ScheduledTaskTrigger -AtStartup

# Create settings (behavior)
$settings = New-ScheduledTaskSettingsSet `
    -AllowStartIfOnBatteries `
    -DontStopIfGoingOnBatteries `
    -StartWhenAvailable `
    -MultipleInstances IgnoreNew

# Register the task
Register-ScheduledTask -TaskName $taskName `
    -Action $action `
    -Trigger $trigger `
    -Settings $settings `
    -Description "Run Tableau Admin Dashboard 24/7" `
    -Force

What This Creates: - Task named TableauAdminDashboard - Runs at system startup - Runs PowerShell script - Script runs app in infinite loop - Auto-restarts on crash

docs.title: Tableau Admin Dashboard - Windows Service Setup Guide
docs.text: Complete automated setup scripts to run the tableau-admin-dashboard as a 24/7 Windows Service.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Windows 11 or Windows Server
  • Python 3.10+ installed
  • Administrator privileges
  • PowerShell 5.0+

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
1. Open PowerShell as Administrator
  2. Right-click PowerShell icon → "Run as Administrator"

  3. Navigate to the dashboard folder: 

    cd "C:\path\to\tableau-admin-dashboard"

  4. Set execution policy (one-time, if needed) 

    Set-ExecutionPolicy -ExecutionPolicy RemoteSigned -Scope CurrentUser -Force

  5. Set up Python environment 

    .\setup-environment.ps1
    This creates the virtual environment and installs all dependencies.

  6. Configure the application 

    notepad config.yaml

  7. Set server_url to your Tableau Server URL
  8. Set site_name (leave empty for "Default")

  9. Save and close

  10. Install and start as Windows Service 

    .\setup-service.ps1
    This will:

  11. Download NSSM (Non-Sucking Service Manager)
  12. Create the service wrapper script
  13. Install the Windows Service
  14. Configure auto-restart on crash
  15. Start the service

  16. Test connectivity

  17. Verify it's running 

    Open browser: http://localhost:5000
    You should see the dashboard setup page.

docs.title: 1. setup-environment.ps1
docs.text:
Purpose: Create Python virtual environment and install dependencies

Usage: 

.\setup-environment.ps1                    # Initial setup
.\setup-environment.ps1 -Reset             # Reset/reinstall dependencies

What it does: - Verifies Python 3.10+ is installed - Creates .venv virtual environment - Installs packages from requirements.txt - Verifies all key packages are available

When to use: - First time installation - After updating requirements.txt - To fix missing dependencies

docs.title: 2. setup-service.ps1
docs.text:
Purpose: Install and configure Windows Service using NSSM

Usage: 

.\setup-service.ps1                        # Install/configure service
.\setup-service.ps1 -Uninstall             # Remove service
.\setup-service.ps1 -SkipNSSMDownload      # Skip NSSM download (if already installed)

What it does: - Downloads NSSM from nssm.cc - Creates run_service.bat wrapper script - Registers Windows Service with auto-restart - Sets service to start automatically on reboot - Starts the service - Tests connectivity

Requires: Administrator privileges

When to use: - First time setup - To reinstall service after removal - To update service configuration

docs.title: 3. manage-service.ps1
docs.text:
Purpose: Quick management commands for the running service

Usage: 

.\manage-service.ps1                       # Show status (default)
.\manage-service.ps1 -Action start         # Start service
.\manage-service.ps1 -Action stop          # Stop service
.\manage-service.ps1 -Action restart       # Restart service
.\manage-service.ps1 -Action logs          # View last 30 lines of logs
.\manage-service.ps1 -Action logs -Follow  # Follow logs in real-time
.\manage-service.ps1 -Action gui           # Open Services GUI
.\manage-service.ps1 -Action uninstall     # Uninstall service

What it shows: - Service status (Running/Stopped) - Start type (Automatic) - Application connectivity test - Log file locations

Requires: Administrator privileges (for start/stop/restart)

When to use: - Daily monitoring - Checking logs - Troubleshooting issues - Managing the service

docs.title: Set Up TLS/HTTPS (Healthcare Recommended)
docs.text:
The app currently runs on HTTP. For healthcare data, use a reverse proxy:

Option 1: IIS (Microsoft Internet Information Services) - Install IIS on Windows - Add reverse proxy role - Configure SSL certificate - Forward traffic to http://localhost:5000

Option 2: nginx - Install nginx - Configure nginx.conf with upstream - Configure SSL certificate - Forward traffic to http://localhost:5000

docs.title: Best Practices & Governance
docs.text: This guide provides recommendations for effective governance and monitoring of your Tableau environment.

docs.title: Daily (5 minutes)
docs.text:
• Check Refresh Health for failed extracts
  • Look for critical Findings or alerts
  • Review any error notifications

docs.title: Weekly (30 minutes)
docs.text:
• Review Workbooks for activity
  • Check Users last login dates
  • Monitor Custom Views creation
  • Review Findings section
  • Verify Health status

docs.title: Monthly (1-2 hours)
docs.text:
• Full audit of Permissions
  • Review stale content
  • Analyze Lineage for optimization opportunities
  • Generate reports for stakeholders
  • Plan maintenance and archival

docs.title: Quarterly (2-4 hours)
docs.text:
• Comprehensive governance review
  • License utilization analysis
  • User access audit
  • Datasource consolidation review
  • Disaster recovery testing

docs.title: Principle of Least Privilege
docs.text:
Rule: Users should have minimum permissions needed for their job.

How to implement: 1. Start with Viewer role (read-only) 2. Upgrade to Creator/Explorer only if needed 3. Regularly audit permissions 4. Remove access when users change roles

docs.title: Recommended Permission Levels
docs.text: Role Typical User Recommended Permissions Admin IT/Tableau admins All permissions Creator Content developers Create, Edit, Share Explorer Power users View, Interact, Download Viewer General users View only

docs.title: Quarterly Permission Audit
docs.text:
1. Go to Permissions
  2. Review all Admin-level users:
  3. Are they still Admin?
  4. Should they be downgraded?
  5. Review high-access Creator accounts
  6. Identify unused accounts to remove

docs.title: Stale Content Policy
docs.text:
Rule: Remove or update workbooks not modified in 90 days.

Process: 1. Go to Workbooks 2. Filter by "Updated" column - find old dates 3. For each stale workbook: - Contact owner - Ask if still needed - Schedule archival or update - Document decision 4. Archive or delete 5. Log action for audit

docs.title: Naming Conventions
docs.text:
Recommendation: Use consistent naming to make content searchable.

Example format: 

[Department] - [Content Type] - [Subject] - [Version]
Finance - Dashboard - Monthly Budget Summary - v2.1

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text: Requirement: Each workbook should have: - Clear description - Owner/contact info - Refresh schedule - Data source information - Last updated date

docs.title: Version Control
docs.text: Best Practice: - Keep only current version active - Archive old versions - Use naming to distinguish versions - Document version history

docs.title: Extract Refresh Health
docs.text:
Goal: 99%+ success rate

Actions: 1. Monitor Refresh Health daily 2. Set alerts for consecutive failures (>2) 3. Investigate failures immediately: - Check source database availability - Verify connection credentials - Review error logs 4. Prevent issues: - Schedule refreshes during off-peak hours - Allow sufficient time between refreshes - Monitor resource usage

docs.title: Datasource Consolidation
docs.text:
Goal: Reduce redundancy and improve performance

Process: 1. Use Lineage to find overlapping datasources 2. Identify opportunities to consolidate 3. Plan migration: - Create unified datasource - Update workbooks to use new source - Archive old datasources 4. Verify performance after consolidation

docs.title: Datasource Documentation
docs.text: Each datasource should include: - Data refresh schedule - Owner contact info - Data source location (database/API) - Last successful refresh time - Known limitations or caveats

docs.title: New User Onboarding
docs.text:
1. Add user to Tableau Server
  2. Assign minimal role (Viewer initially)
  3. Grant access to specific workbooks only
  4. Document decision
  5. Schedule 30-day review

docs.title: Offboarding Process
docs.text:
1. Get notification of departing employee
  2. Review their Permissions in dashboard
  3. Document all access they have
  4. Remove all permissions
  5. Transfer ownership of critical content:
  6. Reassign workbooks
  7. Reassign datasources
  8. Document transfers
  9. Deactivate account
  10. Archive for compliance

docs.title: Inactive User Management
docs.text:
Rule: Remove licenses for users inactive 90+ days

Process: 1. Monthly: Export Users list 2. Filter by Last Login > 90 days 3. Verify they should still be active: - Check with manager - Review their job function 4. Decide on each: - Keep (still needed) - Downgrade (reduce license level) - Remove (no longer needed) 5. Execute changes 6. Document decisions

docs.title: Permission Audit Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] No users have unnecessary Admin role
  • [ ] External users have minimal permissions
  • [ ] Sensitive data access is restricted
  • [ ] Shared content is appropriate
  • [ ] Users only access content for their role
  • [ ] Former employees removed
  • [ ] Access reviewed in past 6 months

docs.title: Data Security Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Encryption: Enable SSL/TLS for all connections
  2. Authentication: Use SSO where possible
  3. Audit Logging: Enable and review audit logs
  4. Sensitive Data: Restrict access to filtered views
  5. Compliance: Follow data retention policies

docs.title: Account Numbers for User Identification
docs.text:
New Feature: BigQuery-synced employee IDs

Use cases: - Compliance Reporting: Track internal vs external usage - User Identification: Quickly match views to employees - HR Integration: Correlate with employee records - Access Auditing: Verify correct employee has access

Where found: - Users section (employee ID for each account) - Custom Views (employee ID of view creator) - Filtered view ( only = @yourorg.com employees)

Learn more about Account Numbers →

docs.title: Key Metrics to Track
docs.text: Metric Threshold Action Failed Extract Refreshes >2 consecutive failures Investigate immediately Stale Workbooks 90+ days without update Contact owner Inactive Users 90+ days no login Plan removal Permission Violations Any overly permissive Schedule audit System Health Any red indicators Check immediately

docs.title: Alert Setup
docs.text:
1. Check your monitoring system for alerts
  2. Configure notifications for:
  3. Extract refresh failures
  4. Permission changes
  5. User access requests
  6. System health issues
  7. Establish escalation path:
  8. First alert → Check dashboard
  9. Multiple failures → Contact owner
  10. Critical issue → Escalate to IT

docs.title: Weekly Status Report
docs.text:
Send to: Governance team/stakeholders

Include: - Extract refresh success rate - New workbooks created - Permissions changes made - Any critical findings - Upcoming maintenance

docs.title: Monthly Governance Report
docs.text:
Send to: Leadership/compliance

Include: - User activity statistics - Permission audit results - Content archival actions - Any security incidents - Recommendations

docs.title: Quarterly Business Review
docs.text:
Meeting: Tableau stakeholders

Topics: - License utilization - Usage trends - Performance metrics - Planned improvements - Budget/resource needs

docs.title: Performance Optimization
docs.text:
1. Use Lineage to find inefficiencies
  2. Consolidate redundant datasources
  3. Archive unused workbooks
  4. Optimize slow extracts:
  5. Reduce data volume
  6. Add incremental refresh
  7. Schedule off-peak
  8. Monitor impact

docs.title: Capacity Planning
docs.text:
1. Track user growth
  2. Monitor extract refresh time
  3. Plan for seasonal peaks
  4. Size infrastructure appropriately
  5. Plan ahead for license needs

docs.title: Disaster Recovery
docs.text:
1. Document critical content:
  2. Workbooks used by executives
  3. Datasources for compliance reporting
  4. High-impact dashboards
  5. Test backup/restore procedures monthly
  6. Document recovery procedures
  7. Train team on recovery process
  8. Plan for failover scenarios

docs.title: Roles & Responsibilities
docs.text:
Tableau Administrator: - Overall system management - Permission management - User provisioning/deprovisioning - Performance optimization - Disaster recovery

Content Owner: - Maintain workbook documentation - Keep content current (update within 90 days) - Remove stale content - Manage data quality - Provide training

Data Steward: - Datasource management - Extract refresh health - Data quality monitoring - Documentation - Performance tuning

Governance Lead: - Compliance monitoring - Permission audits - Policy enforcement - Risk management - Stakeholder communication

docs.title: Decision Tracking
docs.text: Document all major decisions: - Archive decisions (what was archived, why, when) - Permission changes (who, what, why, when) - Datasource consolidations - Major configuration changes - Compliance actions

docs.text:

docs.title: Common Workflows
docs.text: This guide provides step-by-step instructions for common tasks in the Tableau Admin Dashboard.

docs.title: 1. Find Stale Content (Not Updated in 90 Days)
docs.text:
Purpose: Identify workbooks that might be unused or need updating

Steps:

  1. Go to Workbooks
  2. Look at the "Updated" column - note the dates
  3. Alternatively, filter if "Stale" column exists:
  4. Filter Status → Select "Stale"
  5. Review the list:
  6. Check if workbook is still needed
  7. Contact owner to ask if it's still in use
  8. Plan to archive or update
  9. Take action:
  10. Archive if no longer needed
  11. Update if still relevant
  12. Create new version if outdated

Expected Output: - List of workbooks not updated in 90+ days - Owner information - Context for archival decisions

docs.title: 2. Audit User Permissions
docs.text:
Purpose: Ensure users have appropriate access levels

Steps:

  1. Go to Permissions
  2. Filter by specific user:
  3. Look for search/filter options
  4. Enter user name or email
  5. Review what permissions they have:
  6. ✓ (Allowed) - They have this permission
  7. ✗ (Denied) - Explicitly blocked
  8. (blank) - Uses default rules
  9. Identify concerns:
  10. Do they have Admin when only Creator is needed?
  11. Do they have access to sensitive content?
  12. Is access still needed?
  13. Take action:
  14. Discuss with team lead
  15. Adjust permissions if needed
  16. Document the change

Expected Output: - List of all permissions for a user - Identification of unusual or overly permissive access

docs.title: 3. Troubleshoot Data Refresh Failures
docs.text:
Purpose: Identify and fix failing datasource extracts

Steps:

  1. Go to Refresh Health
  2. Look for "Status" column:
  3. Red/Failed = Extract failed to refresh
  4. Green/Success = Successfully refreshed
  5. Yellow/Running = Currently refreshing
  6. Click on a failed datasource
  7. Check details:
  8. When did it fail?
  9. How many times in a row? (Consecutive Failures)
  10. What error message appears?
  11. Investigate causes:
  12. Go to Lineage to understand dependencies
  13. Check if source database is down
  14. Review datasource connection settings
  15. Take action:
  16. Contact datasource owner
  17. Fix database connection if needed
  18. Trigger manual refresh if needed
  19. Set up alerts for failures

Expected Output: - Identified cause of refresh failure - Action plan to fix the issue

docs.title: 4. Understand Data Dependencies
docs.text:
Purpose: See how data flows from source to dashboard

Steps:

  1. Go to Lineage
  2. Click on a workbook you want to understand
  3. You'll see:
  4. Data sources feeding into this workbook
  5. Databases/systems providing the data
  6. Other workbooks depending on same sources
  7. Analyze the chain:
  8. Start: Database/external system
  9. Middle: Published datasource
  10. End: Workbook/Dashboard
  11. Use this to:
  12. Plan maintenance (know what breaks if datasource changes)
  13. Troubleshoot (find where data issues originate)
  14. Optimize (consolidate redundant datasources)

Expected Output: - Visual/text representation of data flow - List of all dependencies

docs.title: 5. Find Who Owns a Workbook
docs.text:
Purpose: Locate the contact for a specific workbook

Steps:

  1. Go to Workbooks
  2. Find the workbook in the list
  3. Look at "Owner" column
  4. Click on owner name (if clickable)
  5. You'll see:
  6. Owner email
  7. Owner contact info
  8. Other workbooks they own
  9. Reach out to owner:
  10. Ask about workbook usage
  11. Request updates if stale
  12. Discuss permissions

Expected Output: - Owner contact information - Context about workbook maintenance

docs.title: 6. Monitor Extract Refresh Performance
docs.text:
Purpose: Track which extracts are healthy and which are failing

Steps:

  1. Go to Refresh Health
  2. Review the table:
  3. Datasource name
  4. Last refresh status
  5. When it last ran
  6. Consecutive failures
  7. Identify problem datasources:
  8. Multiple consecutive failures
  9. Not refreshed recently
  10. Long refresh duration
  11. Analyze trends:
  12. Do failures happen at specific times?
  13. Are certain datasources always failing?
  14. Is performance degrading?
  15. Create action plan:
  16. Fix failing datasources
  17. Optimize slow refreshes
  18. Schedule better refresh times
  19. Set up alerts

Expected Output: - Health assessment of all extracts - List of problem datasources - Prioritized action items

docs.title: 7. Identify Inactive Users
docs.text:
Purpose: Find users who haven't logged in recently

Steps:

  1. Go to Users
  2. Look at "Last Login" column
  3. Identify users who haven't logged in in 90+ days
  4. Cross-reference:
  5. Check if they're supposed to be active
  6. Ask their manager if still needed
  7. Review their permissions in Permissions
  8. Take action:
  9. Remove if no longer needed
  10. Re-activate if person returns
  11. Downgrade license level if appropriate

Expected Output: - List of inactive users - Recommendation for each (keep/remove/downgrade)

docs.title: 8. Identify Custom Views by User
docs.text:
Purpose: Find all custom views created by a specific user

Steps:

  1. Go to Custom Views
  2. Filter by "Owner":
  3. Select specific owner name
  4. Or use search to find user email
  5. View results:
  6. All views created by that user
  7. Which workbooks contain them
  8. Shared or private status
  9. Associated employee account number (if available)
  10. Analyze:
  11. How many views did they create?
  12. Are they shared widely?
  13. Are they still relevant?

Expected Output: - List of custom views by specific user

docs.title: 9. Filter Custom Views by Account Type
docs.text:
Purpose: Separate Mayo employees from external contractors

Steps:

  1. Go to Custom Views
  2. Find the "Account Type" filter (near top)
  3. Choose filter option:
  4. " only" - Shows @yourorg.com accounts with employee IDs
  5. "Non- only" - Shows external accounts
  6. "All accounts" - No filtering
  7. View results:
  8. Mayo: Will show employee account numbers
  9. Non-: Won't have account numbers (external)
  10. Use this for:
  11. Compliance (track internal vs external use)
  12. Reporting (how much content external users create)
  13. Security (audit external access)

    14. Expected Output: - Filtered list of custom views - Clear separation of Mayo vs external users

docs.title: 10. Export Data for Reporting
docs.text:
Purpose: Get data into Excel/CSV for analysis

Steps:

  1. Go to any table view (Workbooks, Users, Custom Views, etc.)
  2. Look for Export or Download button
  3. Choose format:
  4. CSV (comma-separated, opens in Excel)
  5. PDF (for printing)
  6. Click to download
  7. Open file in Excel/Google Sheets
  8. Analyze:
  9. Create pivot tables
  10. Make charts
  11. Send to stakeholders
  12. Archive for compliance

Expected Output: - CSV/PDF file with all data from that view - Ready for analysis in spreadsheet tools

docs.title: 11. Track Content Shared with Specific Users
docs.text:
Purpose: See what content a user has access to

Steps:

  1. Go to Permissions
  2. Filter by user name/email
  3. Review all permission entries:
  4. Shows every workbook/datasource they can access
  5. Shows permission types (View, Edit, Share, etc.)
  6. Analyze access:
  7. Do they need all this access?
  8. Should any be removed?
  9. Are permissions appropriate for their role?
  10. Take action:
  11. Discuss with manager
  12. Remove unnecessary permissions
  13. Document access

Expected Output: - Complete list of user's access rights

docs.title: 12. Monitor User Activity
docs.text:
Purpose: Track who's actually using Tableau

Steps:

  1. Go to Users
  2. Check "Last Login" column:
  3. Recent dates = actively using
  4. Old dates = not using
  5. Never = never logged in
  6. Analyze patterns:
  7. Are users actually engaged?
  8. Are licenses being fully utilized?
  9. Are there cost optimization opportunities?
  10. Report findings:
  11. Identify unused licenses
  12. Plan license reductions
  13. Target training for inactive users
  14. Reallocate seats to new users

Expected Output: - User engagement assessment - Recommendations for license optimization
